main_body: Red barn: a large tiled roof slope with a dormer on top of a plank wall front that has a double X-braced door, two windows and a stone base
top_band: Roof slope with a cream ridge highlight at rows 6-7 (x=24 and x=71, L~220 then 138), then tile rows of L 42-110 through row 56 as one tiled surface; closed at the front by a cream eave line at row 56-57
evidence: The roof is a big foreshortened tile slope, with a bright ridge at the top and a bright eave edge at rows 56-57. A dark shadow row sits under the eave, and below it is the vertical plank wall (rows ~59-89) on a stone base. The door and windows have dark inset frames. It is built like the Beodeul house references: roof slope above, front wall below, no receding side faces.

style.evidence: The roof has a tile pattern with per-tile highlights and about 5 steps, and the outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral). But the whole piece has only 23 distinct colours against 66 and 185 in the references, and a median of 7 colours per tile against 11 and 18. The wall is plain vertical stripes of 2-3 reds. The door braces and window frames are flat light grey, and the stone base is sparse. It reads thinner and flatter than the reference houses, which carry plaster speckle, stone shading and tile variety.
